vocab.definition: add acid → fizzes, CO₂ turns limewater cloudy.
add nitric acid then silver nitrate → coloured precipitate.
add hydrochloric acid then barium chloride → white precipitate.
a negative ion being tested for.

misconceptions.right: AgCl white, AgBr cream, AgI yellow.

misconceptions.wrong: Add barium chloride alone for sulfates.
misconceptions.right: Add dilute HCl first to remove carbonates.
Carbonates are tested with dilute acid + limewater.

infoPanels.title: ANION TEST SUMMARY
workedSteps: Cl⁻ white · Br⁻ cream · I⁻ yellow.
Add the acid first to remove other ions.

questions.text: Describe the test and result for a carbonate. [2 marks]
Describe the test and result for a sulfate. [2 marks]
State the precipitate colours for chloride, bromide and iodide with silver nitrate. [3 marks]
Explain why dilute acid is added before the main test reagent. [2 marks]

questions.secondaryText: A sulfate gives a ______ precipitate with ______ chloride.

questions.text: A solution gives a cream precipitate with AgNO₃. Identify the ion. [1 mark]

footer.tip: Silver halides: Cl⁻ white, Br⁻ cream, I⁻ yellow. Sulfate → white with BaCl₂.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why could a carbonate give a false positive in the sulfate test without acid?
